Subject: SLO gating & concurrency runbook — acceptance criteria and demo window (Kestrel Health)

Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — great context on Kestrel's inference footprint. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an actionable POC plan: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct me if I missed anything):
- Target p95 / p99 end-to-end latency requirements: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms for 512-token generation baseline (currently seeing p95 ~180ms / p99 ~450ms from incumbent).
- Concurrent production load: steady-state 220 rps with 3k daily peak.
- Streaming requirements: partial-token streaming for user typing latency; min chunk latency requirement ~40ms per chunk.
- Throughput expectations: burstable to 500 rps during peak windows for 10–15 minutes.
- Data constraints: no customer PII in test payloads — we'll use synthetic prompts and a 10k prompt sample you mentioned.

What we propose for the POC/demo (high level):
1) 90-minute live demo + 1-hour follow-up run where Redwood runs traffic against a mirrored endpoint.
2) Runbook items: concurrency ramp (0 -> 50 -> 120 -> 220 -> 350 -> 500) over controlled intervals, streaming enabled vs disabled comparisons, and token-length buckets (128 / 256 / 512 / 1024).
3) Acceptance checklist: validate p95/p99 at each bucket, verify streaming chunk latency targets, confirm no more than 1% error increase vs incumbent outputs, and capture token/cost metrics.
4) Required from Kestrel: the 10k-sample prompt set (sanitized), a read-only service account for the test endpoint (or temporary API key), and a short window for cross-team access (SRE + Product).

I've attached a short post-call notes PDF and included a proposed acceptance checklist that Ben will formalize. Can you confirm the SRE contact and a couple of 90-minute windows next week that work for your team?

If the targets above are accurate we'll draft a concrete timeline and DocuSign SOW for the POC scope.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers you listed are what we discussed and reflect internal goals: p95 target 120ms, p99 target 300ms, steady 220 rps, short bursts to ~500 rps.

I've attached a small profiling sample from our current provider (anonymized). Our SRE, Marco Lopez (sre@kestrelhealth.com), is copied on this thread — he'll coordinate the read-only account for the POC.

Preferred times next week: Tuesday (12/8) 10:00–12:30 PT or Thursday (12/10) 13:00–15:30 PT. We prefer the Tuesday window if that works.

One operational note: our compliance team requires that any token-level logs from the POC be retained for 30 days and then auto-deleted — happy to sign an agreement for that.

Best,

Hi Alicia / Marco —

We can take the Tuesday 12/8 10:00–12:30 PT window. Agenda I propose:
- 10:00–10:25: Setup & credential exchange (verify test key + endpoint).
- 10:25–11:10: Live demo — streaming vs non-streaming comparison (short token examples).
- 11:10–11:55: Load-run — concurrency ramp and token-bucketed tests.
- 11:55–12:15: Results review against acceptance checklist.
- 12:15–12:30: Next steps & SOW timeline.

Runbook details (brief):
- Concurrency ramp schedule: 0, 50, 120, 220, 350, 500 with 5–7 minute steady windows.
- Metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end), per-chunk latency for streaming, error rate, cost-per-1k-tokens estimate, and tail latency breakdown.
- Acceptance thresholds: p95 <= 120ms and p99 <= 300ms on 512-token bucket at steady 220 rps; streaming chunk latency <= 60ms 95% of the time.

I've attached a draft SLO acceptance checklist for quick review. Also: Monica will run the observability hook to forward traces and token-cost breakdowns to your SRE Slack during the run.

Thanks — see you Tuesday.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
